Subject: Request: custom uptime & p95 latency commitment for Clearhaven deployment

Hi Logan / Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our engineering leadership is aligning on an aggressive rollout and procurement has asked us to get a firm uptime & latency commitment for contract review. High level:
- Target uptime: 99.995% monthly (our legal/procurement labeled this "critical")
- p95 latency target for core inference path: <= 120ms (typical prompt sizes, token limit ~512)
- Traffic profile: peak batch of ~120 requests/s with occasional spikes to 250r/s for short windows

Attached is a short requirements doc that lists endpoints and SLO prioritization (clearhaven_requirements_20260615.pdf).

Questions for Redwood: what approval path do you need internally to sign off on an exception like this? What operational controls would you require (e.g., reserved pool, canary rollout, dedicated routing, SLA credits)? Also: what does a rollback / fallback look like if latency degrades?

We'd like to move quickly — procurement is hoping to include the commitment in the upcoming master services agreement draft. Can someone outline next steps and an internal owner?

Regards,
Grace Lim | Head of Platform
Clearhaven AI

Subject: RE: Request: custom uptime & p95 latency commitment for Clearhaven deployment

Logan / team — quick feasibility note from Product/Infra perspective.

Short answer: possible, with conditions. Details below.

1) Latency guarantee (p95 <= 120ms):
- For generation workloads our p95 is highly dependent on model selection, prompt length, and batch/kv-cache behavior. For off-the-shelf smaller models (quantized variants) we can meet 120ms p95 across typical prompt sizes if requests are routed to a Dedicated/reserved pool and we enforce token/timeout caps.
- For large open models (e.g., 13B+), p95 at that tail will likely exceed 120ms under load unless we provide isolated prewarmed nodes and restrict concurrency.

2) Uptime (99.995%):
- Achievable operationally if we allocate a reserved capacity cluster in two zones, with automated failover and active health checks. This requires a Dedicated contract or a Hosted+reserved burst add-on (ops & budget dependent).

3) Operational requirements we need from the customer:
- Advance traffic forecast windows (72h preferred) for major spikes so we can scale pre-warmed capacity.
- SLA runbook acceptance: clear definitions of "incidents" vs "degraded performance" and agreed measurement method (which region, which endpoint, sampling windows).
- Access to redacted call traces during incidents for postmortems.

4) Risks / rollback:
- If latency degrades we can automatically route to fallbacks (lower-cost model variant or a cached response), but that will change output characteristics. Customer must approve a fallback policy and error budget.

Ask: Can Sales confirm whether Clearhaven is willing to pay for reserved capacity pricing and the expected committed monthly spend? Without reserved capacity the commitment is too risky.

I'll draft a technical note (one page) and hand to Ops by EOD 16 Jun. Marcus — can you weigh in on model-specific tails and whether we can pre-compile kernels to help p95?

— Sean
VP Product
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.inference
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.inference; Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference>; kimberly_park@redwood.inference
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference; monica_patel@redwood.inference
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: custom uptime & p95 latency commitment for Clearhaven deployment

Adding engineering operational detail.

- Model choices: recommend offering two model tiers to Clearhaven in contract: a "latency tier" (smaller, quantized 7B or trimmed 13B) that we can guarantee p95 <= 120ms when served from reserved capacity; and a "capability tier" (larger models) offered best-effort with an explicit non-guaranteed clause.
- KV cache + prefix caching: for Clearhaven's core flows we can precompute prefix caches for common prompts; this reduces per-token time significantly and helps meet p95. We'll need a short on-boarding period to identify top prompt sets (1-2 weeks).
- Pre-warmed pool sizing: initial reserved pool estimate: 4 x A100-equivalent nodes in two AZs to cover steady-state + spike headroom. Ops cost estimate needed.
- Observability: must instrument a dedicated metric (clearhaven.p95.inference.ms) and surface it in Console; ops must configure alerting at 110ms p95 so we get early warning.

I can deliver a trimmed technical appendix for the draft SLA by EOD 17 Jun.

— Marcus
Director, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Request: custom uptime & p95 latency commitment for Clearhaven deployment

Grace / Ashok — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and next steps from our internal review: 

What we can commit (preliminary, pending legal):
- Uptime: we can offer a 99.995% monthly availability commitment if Clearhaven signs up for a Dedicated reserved capacity configuration (multi-AZ) and accepts the operational runbook we will share.
- Latency: we can guarantee p95 <= 120ms for the agreed inference route if Clearhaven opts into the "latency tier" model variants and we implement the prefix-caching onboarding. For larger models, latency will be best-effort (will be explicitly excluded from the p95 guarantee).

Operational / commercial conditions:
- Reserved capacity commitment (minimum 12-month term) and a base commit to cover the pre-warmed pool. Detailed sizing & cost estimate attached (redwood_draft_sla_v0.1.pdf).
- Agreed fallback policy: on degradation we'll route traffic to the latency tier model or cached responses; customer must accept potential changes in output characteristics during fallback.
- Measurement & reporting: Redwood Console will publish clearhaven.p95.inference.ms and availability metrics; post-incident reports and access to redacted traces included in the runbook.

Next steps:
1) Legal & Commercial to produce contract language — I'll route the draft SLA (attached) to your procurement.
2) Ops to produce runbook and on-call escalation matrix (OPS-482) — target delivery Fri 18 Jun EOD.
3) Kickoff call to agree prompt sets for prefix caching — propose Tue 22 Jun.

I've attached the draft SLA for initial review. If this high-level approach is acceptable, please confirm and we'll escalate a formal MSA redline.

Best,
Logan
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
